title: Getting around
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: a la derecha / a la izquierda / todo recto

rules.text: hay introduces something whose existence is the news and never takes a definite article: ¿Hay una tienda cerca? está locates something both speakers already know: la tienda está cerca. Hay la tienda is the English "there is the shop", and it is wrong.
The polite imperative is built from the I-form with the other vowel: sigo → siga, giro → gire, cruzo → cruce, tomo → tome. It is the shape L3's subjunctive will reuse, so it is worth noticing now.
se plus a he-she verb says "one" — ¿Cómo se va a la plaza? asks how a person gets there without naming anybody. It is the same little se that hides inside se llama.
Transport takes en: voy en autobús, en metro, en tren. English's "by" and Spanish's en both drop the article, so the shape transfers.
a la derecha, a la izquierda and todo recto travel as whole phrases. Learn each as one word rather than assembling it, because the a and the todo inside them are doing nothing you can reuse.
cerca and lejos need de before a place: cerca de la plaza, lejos de aquí. On their own — está cerca — they simply mean near or far with no destination named.

words.note: Feminine despite the -ión ending looking masculine: la estación. The written accent disappears in the plural, estaciones, because the stress no longer needs marking.

sentences.trap: está locates something you both know exists. For asking whether one exists at all, S02 uses hay.
sentences.sound: es-ta-SYON, stressed on the last syllable, which is why it carries an accent.

variations.display: Perdone, ¿dónde está la plaza?
variations.cue: Excuse me, where's the square?
variations.changed: the same question about another place

variations.display: Disculpe, ¿dónde está el metro?
variations.cue: Sorry, where's the metro?
variations.changed: M1's other opener, and a masculine place

variations.display: ¿Dónde están las tiendas?
variations.cue: Where are the shops?
variations.changed: a plural subject takes están

mistake.why: hay never takes a definite article. For a place you both know exists, it is ¿dónde está…?

sentences.usage: The first sentence of most conversations a traveller has. Perdone opens it; the question does the rest.
sentences.mnemonic: está points at a known place; hay announces an unknown one.

words.note: Masculine: el banco. The same word covers a bank and a park bench, and the sentence says which.
On its own it means nearby with no place named. To name one it takes de: cerca de la plaza, the phrase M7 of the level below taught.

sentences.trap: hay is one word for "there is" and "there are" alike, and it never changes: hay una tienda, hay dos tiendas.
sentences.sound: SER-ka in most of Spain the c before e is a th; across Latin America it is an s. Both are standard.

variations.display: ¿Hay una tienda cerca?
variations.cue: Is there a shop nearby?
variations.changed: a feminine place, and hay does not move

variations.display: ¿Hay dos estaciones aquí?
variations.cue: Are there two stations here?
variations.changed: more than one, and hay still does not move

variations.display: Sí, hay un banco muy cerca.
variations.cue: Yes, there's a bank very close by.
variations.changed: the answer, with muy in front of cerca

mistake.why: hay asks whether a thing exists, so it cannot take el. Either ¿Hay un banco…? or ¿Dónde está el banco?

sentences.usage: How you find anything in a town you do not know. The answer usually comes back as directions.
sentences.mnemonic: hay never counts and never takes the.

words.note: The polite imperative of seguir, built from the I-form sigo with the vowel swapped: sigo → siga. Every polite imperative in this module is made the same way.
Two words that travel as one. Neither half is reusable — the todo here is not counting anything — so learn the phrase whole.

sentences.trap: There is no polite verb ending to add. The imperative changes its vowel and that is the whole of it.
sentences.sound: SI-ga, with a hard g. REK-to, with the c fully said.

variations.display: Siga todo recto y gire a la derecha.
variations.cue: Go straight on and turn right.
variations.changed: two instructions joined by y

variations.display: Siga por favor, está muy cerca.
variations.cue: Carry on please, it's very close.
variations.changed: the instruction with a reassurance after it

variations.display: Todo recto, no está lejos.
variations.cue: Straight on, it isn't far.
variations.changed: the phrase alone, with the verb left out

mistake.why: sigue is the tú imperative. To a stranger in the street it is siga.

sentences.usage: Said to a stranger, and heard far more often than it is spoken by a learner.
sentences.mnemonic: Take the I-form, swap the vowel, and you are being polite.

sentences.display: Gire a la derecha en la esquina.
sentences.literal: Turn(polite) to the right at the corner.

words.note: The polite imperative of girar, from giro with the vowel swapped — the same recipe as siga.
Three words as one. The a inside it is not the a of M4's a las ocho, which is why the phrase is learnt whole.
The corner of a street. Feminine: la esquina.

sentences.trap: en la esquina, not a la esquina. Spanish puts you AT the corner and turns you TO the right.
sentences.sound: HI-re, with the g before an e said as a Spanish j — a breathy h.

variations.display: Gire a la izquierda en la plaza.
variations.cue: Turn left at the square.
variations.changed: the other direction, at another landmark

variations.display: Gire a la derecha y siga todo recto.
variations.cue: Turn right and go straight on.
variations.changed: the two instructions in the other order

variations.display: La tienda está a la derecha.
variations.cue: The shop is on the right.
variations.changed: the phrase locating something rather than instructing

mistake.display: Gire la derecha en la esquina.
mistake.why: The phrase is a la derecha. Dropping the a leaves you turning the right itself.

sentences.usage: The commonest instruction anyone gives. Learn to hear it before you learn to say it.
sentences.mnemonic: You turn TO a side and stand AT a corner.

sentences.display: La plaza está a la izquierda.
sentences.cue: The square is on the left.
sentences.literal: The square is to the left.

words.note: The open square at the middle of a Spanish town, and the place most directions end at. Feminine: la plaza.
The partner of a la derecha, and it travels whole in exactly the same way.

sentences.trap: The same phrase says "turn left" after gire and "on the left" after está. Spanish uses one phrase where English uses two.
sentences.sound: is-KYER-da. The z of izquierda is the same th or s as in cerca, and the qu is a plain k.

variations.display: La estación está a la derecha.
variations.cue: The station is on the right.
variations.changed: the other side, the same frame

variations.display: El banco está a la izquierda.
variations.cue: The bank is on the left.
variations.changed: a masculine place, and nothing else moves

variations.display: Está a la izquierda, muy cerca.
variations.cue: It's on the left, very close.
variations.changed: the subject dropped, as Spanish does once it is known

mistake.display: La plaza es a la izquierda.
mistake.why: Where something is takes estar: está a la izquierda. ser would be claiming the square IS the left.

sentences.usage: The other half of every exchange in this module — you ask, and this is what comes back.
sentences.mnemonic: Position is always estar, whichever side it is on.

sentences.cue: How do you get to the square?
sentences.literal: How one goes to the square?

words.note: Names nobody in particular. ¿Cómo se va…? asks how a person gets there. It is the same se that hides inside se llama, doing its own job for once.
The he-she-usted form of ir, whose voy, vas and vamos M6 of the level below already taught.

sentences.trap: No subject at all, and the question is about you. English needs "you" or "one" and Spanish needs neither.
sentences.sound: The whole question runs together — KO-mo-se-VA — with one stress on cómo and one on va.

variations.display: ¿Cómo se va a la estación?
variations.cue: How do you get to the station?
variations.changed: another destination

variations.display: ¿Cómo se va al metro?
variations.cue: How do you get to the metro?
variations.changed: a plus el fuses into al, as it always does

variations.display: Se va a la plaza en autobús.
variations.cue: You get to the square by bus.
variations.changed: the answer, in the same subjectless shape

mistake.why: Without se this asks how HE or SHE gets there. The se is what makes the question general.

sentences.usage: The single most useful way to ask directions, because it needs no verb form you do not already have.
sentences.mnemonic: se stands in for everybody and nobody.

words.note: The polite imperative of tomar, from tomo. In Spain coja is commoner for catching a bus; tomar is understood everywhere and is what this course writes.
Masculine: el autobús. The accent goes when the plural adds a syllable — autobuses.
The opposite of cerca and it behaves the same way: lejos on its own, lejos de la plaza to name the place. It ends in -s in the singular and never changes.

sentences.trap: lejos already ends in -s and is not a plural. There is no lejo.
sentences.sound: ow-to-BUS with the accent on the last syllable. LE-hos, with the j said as a breathy h.

variations.display: Tome el metro, no está lejos.
variations.cue: Take the metro, it isn't far.
variations.changed: another way of getting there

variations.display: Está muy lejos de aquí.
variations.cue: It's very far from here.
variations.changed: lejos de naming what it is far from

variations.display: No está lejos, está muy cerca.
variations.cue: It isn't far, it's very close.
variations.changed: the two words of the module set against each other

mistake.why: Distance is a position, so it takes estar: está lejos.

sentences.usage: Given as advice rather than as an order. The second half is why you are being told.
sentences.mnemonic: cerca and lejos both take estar, because both are positions.

sentences.display: El metro está cerca de aquí.
sentences.literal: The metro is near of here.

words.note: Masculine: el metro. The same word in Madrid, Mexico City and Buenos Aires.

sentences.trap: cerca de, not cerca a. The de is not optional once a place is named.
sentences.sound: ME-tro, two beats, with the tr said as one quick tap.

variations.display: La plaza está cerca de la estación.
variations.cue: The square is near the station.
variations.changed: two named places instead of aquí

variations.display: El banco está lejos de aquí.
variations.cue: The bank is far from here.
variations.changed: the opposite distance, same frame

variations.display: Está cerca, no está lejos.
variations.cue: It's close, it isn't far.
variations.changed: both words with no place named at all

mistake.why: cerca takes de before what it is near: cerca de aquí.

sentences.usage: Reassurance. It is what a local says when they can see you are worried about the distance.
sentences.mnemonic: Name the place and you owe it a de.

sentences.display: Cruce la calle y siga todo recto.
sentences.cue: Cross the street and go straight on.
sentences.literal: Cross(polite) the street and continue(polite) all straight.

words.note: The polite imperative of cruzar, from cruzo — and the z becomes c in front of an e, which is a spelling rule and not a sound change.
Feminine: la calle. The ll is a y sound in nearly all of the Spanish-speaking world.

sentences.trap: cruzo has a z and cruce has a c. Spanish never writes ze, so the letter changes to keep the sound.
sentences.sound: KRU-se, and the ll of calle is the y of "yes" — KA-ye.

variations.display: Cruce la plaza y gire a la derecha.
variations.cue: Cross the square and turn right.
variations.changed: a different thing crossed, a different turn

variations.display: No cruce aquí, la estación está lejos.
variations.cue: Don't cross here, the station is far.
variations.changed: the negative imperative, which needs no extra word

variations.display: Siga y cruce la calle.
variations.cue: Carry on and cross the street.
variations.changed: the two instructions swapped

mistake.why: A z never stands before an e in Spanish: cruce. The sound is unchanged; only the letter moves.

sentences.usage: Half of any real set of directions. Notice that both verbs are polite imperatives and neither has a pronoun.
sentences.mnemonic: z before e turns into c, every time.

sentences.display: Es la primera calle a la derecha.
sentences.cue: It's the first street on the right.
sentences.literal: Is the first street to the right.

words.note: An ordinal, and it agrees like any adjective: la primera calle, el primer libro — where primero loses its -o in front of a masculine noun, exactly as grande becomes gran.

sentences.trap: primera goes IN FRONT of the noun, unlike almost every other adjective in this level. Ordinals and numbers are the exception.
sentences.sound: pri-ME-ra, with one tapped r in the middle and another at the start.

variations.display: Es la segunda calle a la izquierda.
variations.cue: It's the second street on the left.
variations.changed: the next street along, the other side

variations.display: Tome la primera calle a la derecha.
variations.cue: Take the first street on the right.
variations.changed: the same information given as an instruction

variations.display: La primera tienda está muy cerca.
variations.cue: The first shop is very close.
variations.changed: the ordinal counting something other than a street

mistake.display: Es la calle primera a la derecha.
mistake.why: An ordinal stands in front of its noun: la primera calle.

sentences.usage: The way directions actually end. Everything before it tells you where to start.
sentences.mnemonic: Numbers go first, in both senses.

comprehensionPool.display: Gire a la derecha en la esquina.
La plaza está a la izquierda.
comprehensionPool.cue: The square is on the left.
How do you get to the station?

comprehensionPool.display: El metro está cerca de aquí.
Cruce la calle y siga todo recto.
comprehensionPool.cue: Cross the street and go straight on.

comprehensionPool.display: Es la primera calle a la derecha.

comprehensionPool.display: No está lejos, está muy cerca.
